profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle, a two-part data center campus in Tukwila, King County, Washington, marketed by the operator as the West Coast's largest privately owned data center campus. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in this same Tukwila location became SDC Seattle Building 5, prompting Sabey's pivot into the data center industry. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Seattle page, the Tukwila campus totals more than a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure not broken out per individual building and not applied to any single structure here. Aggregator sourcing indicates the campus actually comprises two separately addressed sub-campuses: Intergate.East, at a street range of 3311 to 3511 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168, spanning roughly 1.2 million square feet; and Intergate.West, at 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, built in 1999 and spanning roughly 173,000 square feet.

This building, Intergate.East Building 4, was previously misidentified in this registry as a Digital Realty facility. A DatacenterHawk listing titled "Sabey Data Centers Intergate.East Building 4," an exact match to this building's own designation, together with independently agreeing PeeringDB and DataCenterJournal listings, confirms Sabey as the current operator at 3433 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA. No record of a Digital Realty acquisition of this specific Sabey campus was found; the operator field on this row was corrected accordingly, with Digital Realty preserved as a former operator of record rather than deleted, since Intergate is Sabey's own registered campus brand and Digital Realty's own confirmed Seattle-area facility is separately branded SEA1.

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 43 (Digital Realty missing-address campaign): found this rows Intergate brand name belongs to Sabey Data Centers, not Digital Realty, matched an exact Building 4 designation to a specific address under Sabey, and corrected the top level operator field accordingly, preserving Digital Realty as former_operator per this registrys standard policy.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, recorded in this registry as a Digital Realty facility named Intergate Seattle East Building 4 in Tukwila, WA, is a significant correction rather than a simple address add. Intergate is Sabey Data Centers own registered campus brand, not Digital Realtys, and this operators own confirmed current Seattle area facility is separately branded SEA1, not Intergate. A datacenterHawk listing titled Sabey Data Centers Intergate.East Building 4, an exact match to this rows own Building 4 designation, gives 3433 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA, and independently agreeing PeeringDB and DataCenterJournal listings confirm Sabey as the operator of this same Intergate.East campus. This session found no record of Digital Realty ever having acquired this specific Sabey campus, so this may represent either a past genuine change of operator this session could not further document, or an original labeling error in this registry, rather than a confirmed acquisition. Per this registrys standard ownership change policy, the top level operator field on this row was updated from Digital Realty to Sabey Data Centers, with Digital Realty preserved as former_operator rather than deleted, and ownership_verified_on set to todays date. The rows own name still reads Intergate Seattle East Building 4 and was left unchanged, since it already correctly reflects the Sabey brand.

profile.facility_type_note: The Westin Building at 2001 Sixth Avenue, downtown Seattle (Digital Realty's SEA10), is one of the most important internet exchange and carrier hotel buildings on the US West Coast, historically known as the Westin Building Exchange. Digital Realty acquired a controlling stake in the building, per Data Center Frontier and Commercial Property Executive coverage of the transaction. The Intergate facility in Tukwila is a separate building from the downtown Westin Building; Digital Realty also operates a facility (SEA1) at 3433 S 120th Place in the Seattle/Tukwila area per datacenterHawk.

reading.body:
Intergate Seattle East Building 4 is a colocation facility in Tukwila, Washington, operated by Sabey Data Centers. The facility's critical IT load in megawatts is not confirmed from a tier-1 source in available specifications. Without published power capacity, the number of racks or accelerators this building can host cannot be calculated.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, of which only 3 have published power specifications totaling 60 MW. This facility ranks third among published capacity in the state, meaning two other facilities in Washington publish higher individual power draws. The state's low rate of published specifications means most facilities in the region, including this one, operate without disclosed capacity figures in the public record.

Sabey Data Centers operates this facility as part of its Intergate campus brand in the Seattle metropolitan area. The building's role in the regional AI infrastructure depends on specifications not yet published by the operator. Readers assessing AI scaling constraints in the Pacific Northwest should note that published power data covers only a small fraction of Washington's data center footprint.
